deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft addendum ('Zusatz zu pag. 1') to the opening of Riemann's Göttingen dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse' (1851). The previous page is a Latin/German outline of the dissertation's first articles. The published Art. 1 defines continuity only verbally ('w ändert sich stetig'). This addendum makes that definition precise.

(1) Definition, infinitesimal form. 'z changes continuously with x between x=a and x=b' means: in [a,b], every infinitely small change of x produces an infinitely small change of z. This is Cauchy-style language.

(2) Definition, 'more graspable' form. For every given ε>0 one can choose α>0 such that, within any x-interval of length <α (inside [a,b]), the difference of two values of z never exceeds ε. In modern notation: ∀ε>0 ∃α>0 ∀x,x'∈[a,b]: |x−x'|<α ⇒ |z(x)−z(x')| ≤ ε. Note that α depends only on ε, not on the location. This is exactly uniform continuity on [a,b], not pointwise continuity.

(3) Consequence. 'Continuity of a function thereby (hienach) always entails its constant finiteness', i.e. boundedness, even where this is not stated explicitly. Implicit proof (mine): fix ε=1 and its α. Cut [a,b] into N = ceil((b−a)/α)+1 subintervals of length <α. Chaining gives |z(x)−z(a)| ≤ N for all x, so z is bounded on [a,b].

(4) Pencil paragraph, partly struck through. It reads roughly: 'Wir begnügen uns, in Bezug auf diesen Gegenstand auf die zu Art. 3 citirte [Gauss'sche] Abhandlung und auf die Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas art. 13 zu verweisen.' A deleted bibliographic tail reads 'in den Comment. Gott. rec. T. VI'. This is a citation note for the material on conformal (angle-preserving) mappings and on lengths and isometric bending of surfaces. Art. 3 of the dissertation cites Gauss's Copenhagen prize memoir on conformal representation (1825); Disq. gen. art. 13 treats lengths on surfaces and their invariance under bending. No mathematics is derived in this paragraph.
errors: No mathematical error. Riemann presents the ε–α form as merely a 'more graspable' restatement of the infinitesimal one. Read pointwise, the infinitesimal version is equivalent to the uniform ε–α version on a closed bounded interval only by Heine's theorem (compactness), which is not proved or mentioned here.

The boundedness claim ('hienach') is correct given the uniform formulation actually written. It would not follow from pointwise continuity on a non-closed interval (e.g. 1/x on (0,1]). On a closed interval it would need a compactness argument.

results.what: ε–α definition of continuity of z(x) on [a,b], in uniform form: |x−x'|<α ⇒ |z(x)−z(x')| ≤ ε for all x,x' in the interval
results.usually_credited_to: Bolzano (1817) and Cauchy (1821) for continuity; uniform continuity made explicit by Dirichlet (lectures 1854), Weierstrass (lectures c.1861) and Heine (1872)

results.what: A continuous (in this sense) function on [a,b] is bounded
results.modern_name: boundedness of (uniformly) continuous functions on a compact interval

results.what: Reference to Gauss's conformal-mapping memoir and Disq. gen. circa superficies curvas art. 13
results.modern_name: bibliographic note (conformal maps; intrinsic geometry of surfaces)

deep.surprise_reason: A precise ε–α definition of continuity, in uniform form, with boundedness derived from it, in a draft of the 1851 dissertation is a notable unpublished detail; the printed text only gives a verbal definition. It is not a new result, though. Cauchy and Bolzano had such definitions, Riemann was a student of Dirichlet, and he uses ε-style arguments in his 1854 Habilitation on trigonometric series. Historians of Riemann's dissertation drafts (e.g. Laugwitz, Neuenschwander) may already have noted it.

checkable.asserts: x**2 on [0,1] satisfies Riemann's uniform condition with alpha = epsilon/3
Equals oo: 1/x on (0,1] is pointwise continuous but violates the uniform ε–α condition, since points at distance x/2 have values differing by 1/(3x)
Bound on |z(x)-z(a)| obtained by chaining the uniform condition over subintervals of length < alpha, which proves boundedness

transcription_corrections: Pencil paragraph is better read: 'Wir begnügen uns, in Bezug auf diesen Gegenstand auf die zu Art. 3 citirte [Gauss'sche] Abhandlung und auf die disquis. generales circa superf. curvas art. 13 zu verweisen'. 'und [?] kann [?]' is likely a misreading, and the interlinear '{+jenen zweit Gauß'schen+}' likely reads 'jener [zweiten] Gauss'schen'.
'circ.' should be 'circa'. The struck phrase 'in den Comment. Gott. rec. T. VI' is correctly identified as deleted.
Main text transcription is essentially correct. 'nie > ε' means ≤ ε.
